plan.notes: Source: official NJCU catalog archive program page (PDF): http://catalog.njcu.edu/archives/2022-2023/undergraduate/arts-sciences/computer-science/computer-science-bs/computer-science-bs.pdf. Catalog year 2022-2023 is the most recent official NJCU catalog year publishing a full term-by-term 8-semester sequence; the current live catalog page for 'Computer Science, B.S.' (https://catalog.njcu.edu/undergraduate/arts-sciences/computer-science/computer-science-bs/) only lists a major-courses-only plan grid totaling 52 credits with no General Education tiers, insufficient for a full degree plan, so the 2022-2023 full sequence was transcribed. Transcription: manual, semester by semester from the archived program PDF's plan-of-study grid. Credit totals: the PDF prints 'Total Credits 120-125'; the catalog degree minimum is 120. total_credits is set to 120 using the minimum values of variable-credit courses (ENGL 101/102 listed 4-6, MATH 175/165 listed 3-4); students placing into more composition/ESL credit combinations can reach up to 125. Per-semester minimums: 16, 17, 15, 15, 15, 15, 12, 15 = 120. Catalog footnotes: (1) INTD 180 is used to satisfy a General Education Tier I course; (2) MATH 192, CS 214, and CS 215 are used to satisfy Tier II Scientific and Quantitative Inquiries for CS majors. The four 'Computer Science Elective 3XX or 4XX' slots map to the PDF's Advanced Major Electives: select 12 credits from CS 302, CS 355, CS 360, CS 365, CS 401, CS 402, CS 404, CS 405, CS 407, CS 408, CS 409, CS 410, CS 417, CS 420, CS 430, CS 599, SPFD XXXX. Major rules printed in the catalog: 2.5 minimum GPA in all courses credited toward the major; grade of C or above in all major courses including MATH 192 and MATH 193; admission to the track requires a minimum grade of C in MATH 175 or its equivalent. Prereq evidence comes only from official NJCU course descriptions ('CS 102 is a continuation of CS 101', 'CS 203 is a continuation of CS 202', 'CS 351 uses the concepts and techniques developed in CS 350'); all other courses carry no stated prereq in the source and sequence order alone was not used to invent prereqs. The PDF grid spells the INTD 180 title 'Computers Tools for Science and Math'; transcribed as printed.
